- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤-0.33), model often underestimates; adjust upward by 1–3% to account for potential rebound.  
- Model consistently overreacts to recent price spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), leading to overshoot; apply a 2–5 day lag correction by smoothing out sharp peaks.  
- If true outcome shows mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 65–70), model tends to hold or overpredict; reduce forecast by 2–4% for next 3–5 days.  
- For 30-day horizon, model often fails to capture sentiment-driven momentum shifts; weight sentiment history more heavily in the last 5–7 days for adjustment.  
- If sentiment turns sharply positive after a dip, model often misses the rally; add a 1–2% upward bias to forecast if sentiment >0.75 for 2+ consecutive days.
